# Fix a failing test

**If the harness failed too, start there**: it tests the suite's own checks and actions on a page of
its own; when it fails, every other failure is suspect. Rebuilding the suite puts it back.

Then read the evidence: `cypress/failures/<spec>/<test>/steps.txt` (the steps, the failed one marked,
why, the URL and title), `page.html`, `console.txt` (the site's script errors, often the real cause),
and the screenshot in `cypress/screenshots/`. `npm run open` replays a test step by step.

| The failure says | Most likely | Do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `... did not load! URL was X, expected Y` | the site moved the page, or the link | check KNOWN-ISSUES.md; ask if the move is intended |
| `The locator ... is not valid` | a typo in the XPath or CSS: a missing bracket or quote | fix it, and check it with suite locate against the page as crawled |
| `note: X is the right page ..., but had not finished loading after 30 s; still loading: ...` (not a failure) | a slow part of the page: another site's frame, a video, an image | the page passed; the note names what held it back |
| `Timed out after waiting 30000ms for your remote page to load` | cy.visit() waits for the load event, and Cypress fails it | a real finding for this page; or raise pageLoadTimeout |
| `... did not load! Title was ...` | the site changed its titles | rebuild from a new crawl |
| `Expected the X to be shown, but it was not` | a broken locator, or the site changed | find it in a saved page and fix the locator |

A generated locator is outside YOURS blocks: don't edit it. Rebuild from a new crawl, or add a
corrected constant in the elements block and use that. What the site does wrong goes in KNOWN-ISSUES.md.
